messages:
incident-bot: PAGERDUTY: P1 - Multi-region traffic anomalies detected. us-west-2 -> increased 5xx, cross-region routing errors. Pager: matt (oncall). Incident link: https://pd.example/INC12345 :rotating_light:

matt (oncall): seeing ~30% 5xx for hosted-api requests in us-west-2. Customers reporting timeouts, spike in retries. Cloud provider notice?

alisha (SRE): pulling provider status now. also checking ALB/NLB health. can someone run a quick curl against /health for a few replicas?

ben (infra): I see provider alert for us-west-2 networking — partial internal routing flap. AWS status says "Intermittent cross-AZ connectivity degraded". https://status.aws/incident/xyz

maria (platform): confirming health checks failing intermittently on ALBs in us-west-2. Target groups show some targets UNHEALTHY but not a full group down. Could be AZ-level packet loss.

ryan (eng): throwing a quick probe from eu-central and us-east api test runners:
```
# from us-east runner
curl -v https://api.redwood.example/health -H 'Host: api-us-west-2.redwood.example'
# results: TCP handshake delays, then 502s
```

matt (oncall): paging oncall chain, tagging leadership. @jessica (CSM) heads-up for affected customers. I'm going to open incident channel #inc-1793334444.

jessica (CSM): got it, I'll notify top-tier customers and post templated note: "We are experiencing regional issues in us-west-2; we're actively failing traffic to healthy regions and will update with ETA."

alisha (SRE): quick diagnostics:
```
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:us-west-2:... | jq '.TargetHealthDescriptions[] | {id: .Target.Id, state: .TargetHealth.State, reason: .TargetHealth.Reason}'
```
Result: ~40% of targets show "unhealthy" with reason "Connection timed out".

ben (infra): checked connection draining on NLBs — some targets stuck in draining state for >10m due to in-flight connections and BGP flaps. deregistration-delay still at 300s.

matt (oncall): immediate mitigation options? can we shift traffic to us-east-1 weighted failover?

maria (platform): yes, route53 has weighted records and failover policy. TTL is 60s for api*. Changing weights will steer traffic but DNS caches may honor previous records for a minute or two. Also need to scale up us-east target groups before shifting to avoid overload.

alisha (SRE): proposed runbook (short):
1) scale up us-east target group by +50%
2) lower Route53 weight for us-west to 10% and raise us-east to 90% and set health-check failover if possible
3) set deregistration-delay on us-west NLBs to 30s to force faster drain (risk: may drop some in-flight requests)
4) monitor error rates and latencies, start rollback if errors in new region exceed safe thresholds

matt (oncall): I'm IC. alisha/ben you have action on infra/traffic shift. ryan monitor application logs for 5xx patterns. maria coordinate DNS change and confirm TTL. jessica will update customers.

ben (infra): scaling us-east ASG now. running:
```
aws autoscaling set-desired-capacity --auto-scaling-group-name redwood-api-us-east --desired-capacity 180
```
Scaling up targets and prewarming added instances.

alisha (SRE): lowering deregistration delay on us-west NLBs:
```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:us-west-2:... --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=30
```
Applied to both AZs in us-west-2. Expect more dropped in-flight but will speed traffic shift. :grimacing: 

maria (platform): pushing Route53 weight change now (console + API). Old: us-west=60 us-east=40. New: us-west=10 us-east=90.
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-east-1","Weight":90,"AliasTarget":{...}}},{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-2","Weight":10,"AliasTarget":{...}}}]}'
```
Change submitted. TTL 60s.

ryan (eng): seeing initial drop in overall request volume to us-west. us-east inbound increasing. Logs show 200s mostly from us-east, but a handful of 502s due to retries hitting problematic us-west endpoints.

matt (oncall): monitoring metrics dashboard: 5xx overall dropped from 30% -> 8% in last 3 minutes. latency stable in us-east but slightly elevated. Good so far.

alisha (SRE): also noticed Route53 health check for us-west failing intermittently - enabling failover profile so if health check fails fully we cut to 0%. Doing that now.

ben (infra): deployed a temporary BGP route filter workaround with cloud provider support to avoid backhauling loop for us-west AZ B, provider acknowledged and applied a fix on their edge. They expect propagation in ~4-8 minutes.

maria (platform): DNS change TTL expired for many resolvers; traffic now ~95% to us-east within 6 minutes. Monitoring for capacity pressure.

jessica (CSM): sent update to customers: "We've shifted traffic away from the affected region and are monitoring. Expected restoration to full capacity in ~30-60m. We'll send follow-up when provider confirms full network restoration."

ryan (eng): running synthetic checks for critical flows (auth, embeddings, streaming). Auth & embeddings green in us-east; streaming shows occasional dropouts attributed to long-lived TCP sessions that were mid-shift.

matt (oncall): exec summary for incident channel: us-west-2 experienced AZ-level networking degradation that caused ELB target health churn and stuck draining targets. We shifted DNS weights to fail traffic to us-east, reduced draining delay, scaled up us-east, and engaged provider. Early mitigation successful, errors reduced to acceptable levels.

alisha (SRE): next steps: postmortem, revert temporary infra changes (reset deregistration-delay, ASG downscale), validate failover runbook and increase Route53 health-check aggressiveness for quicker automatic failover.

ben (infra): will revert deregistration delay to 300s once provider confirms stable BGP. Scheduling downscale of extra us-east capacity after 45m of steady metrics.

matt (oncall): handing off to alisha for monitoring and postmortem. I'll clear PD and mark incident as active -> mitigated. Thanks all. :pray:

alisha (SRE): taking postmortem owner. capturing timelines, config diffs, and customer impact. initial severity: P1 -> mitigated.

maria (platform): provider posted follow-up 10m ago saying root cause isolated to an AZ edge switch and they completed repairs; they will publish timeline.

jessica (CSM): preparing customer follow-up with timeline and RCA once we have postmortem.

matt (oncall): closing real-time action. I'll leave channel open for follow-ups. If anyone sees regression, re-alert PD.

incident-bot: Incident status updated: Mitigated. Incident channel: #inc-1793334444. Postmortem owner: alisha (SRE).
